second_edition.licence: UCLouvain repository item states CC BY 4.0
second_edition.legal_access_status: Lawful open institutional-repository access. The repository explicitly says the second edition was still being written and needed polishing; it should not be represented as a finalized commercial edition.

third_edition.licence: CC BY-SA 3.0 Unported, as stated in the official source repository
third_edition.legal_access_status: Lawful open access in HTML, source, PDF and EPUB forms through the official project.

fourth_edition.licence: Not independently fixed for a completed fourth-edition release in this audit
fourth_edition.legal_access_status: The official project reports that fourth-edition preparation began in September 2025; it should not yet be cited as a completed edition.

bonaventure_verdict.relevance: The work is highly relevant to RC: it covers data-link reliability, medium access, Ethernet/Wi-Fi, IP, routing, transport, congestion and network applications, with exercises and labs. Relevance does not establish FEUP adoption.

confidence.overall_adoption_verdict: high for 'not verified as used'; the evidence cannot prove universal non-use outside public records

courses.name: Compilers
courses.status_note: 2026/2027 bibliography not treated as populated; this is the latest verified public list.

books.title: Engineering a Compiler
books.access_detail: Publisher purchase/e-book or lawful library access
books.relevance: Directly supports compiler structure, lexical and syntax analysis, semantic analysis, intermediate representations, optimization, register allocation and code generation—the central COMP syllabus and programming project.
books.notes: SIGARRA lists only Keith D. Cooper and does not state an edition. Elsevier identifies Cooper and Torczon as co-authors and identifies the corresponding early work as the 1st edition. Elsevier's listed first-edition print/e-book ISBNs do not exactly match SIGARRA's ISBN, so the edition identification is strong but the FEUP ISBN should be treated as potentially mistyped.

books.title: Compilers: Principles, Techniques, and Tools
books.access_detail: Publisher purchase/e-text or lawful library access
books.relevance: Provides a broad reference for scanning, parsing, semantic analysis, runtime environments, intermediate code, optimization and target-code generation.

books.title: Modern Compiler Implementation in Java
books.access_detail: Publisher purchase or lawful library access
books.relevance: Especially relevant to COMP's Java-based implementation work, covering front ends, type checking, intermediate representations, instruction selection, liveness and register allocation.
books.notes: SIGARRA names only Andrew Wilson Appel and gives ISBN 0-521-82060-X; Cambridge metadata for that ISBN includes Jens Palsberg and identifies the second edition.

courses.name: Computer Graphics
courses.status_note: 2026/2027 bibliography not treated as populated; this is the latest verified public list.

books.title: Introdução à Computação Gráfica
books.access_detail: Publisher purchase; publisher-authorized descriptive/sample material only
books.relevance: The publisher describes coverage of geometric transformations, scene modelling, geometric processing, clipping, illumination, shading, raster operations and photorealism, closely matching CG's 2D/3D modelling and rendering syllabus.

books.title: Computer Graphics, C Version
books.access_detail: Lawful used-book or library access; no authorized open full text verified
books.relevance: Supports classical rasterization, transformations, viewing, modelling, illumination and rendering algorithms covered by CG.
books.notes: SIGARRA abbreviates the title to 'Computer graphics' and lists only Donald Hearn. The ISBN identifies the C Version, second edition, co-authored with M. Pauline Baker.

books.title: Introduction to Computer Graphics
books.access_detail: Authorized preview where available, lawful used-book purchase, or library access
books.relevance: A broad introduction to graphics systems, modelling, transformations, viewing, rasterization, interaction and rendering. It was mandatory in the cited MIEIC occurrence but is only complementary in current LEIC.

courses.name: Parallel and Distributed Computing
courses.status_note: 2026/2027 bibliography not treated as populated; this is the latest verified public list.

books.title: Distributed Systems
books.access_detail: The authors' site offers a personalized downloadable copy after an e-mail request and also links supporting material.
books.relevance: Directly covers architectures, processes, communication, naming, coordination, replication and fault tolerance, matching CPD's distributed-systems half.

books.title: Parallel Programming in C with MPI and OpenMP
books.edition: edition not stated; illustrated international edition
books.access_detail: Commercial book or library access; the author provides lawful supplementary material, not an open full-text edition.
books.relevance: Directly supports design, implementation and benchmarking of parallel C programs using shared-memory OpenMP and distributed-memory MPI.

books.title: Distributed Systems: Concepts and Design
books.access_detail: Publisher, used-book, or library access
books.relevance: Provides conceptual treatment of distributed architectures, communication, naming, synchronization, replication, consistency and fault tolerance.
books.notes: SIGARRA lists only George Coulouris and shortens the title to 'Distributed systems'; the ISBN identifies the full title and co-authors.

books.title: Distributed Systems: Principles and Paradigms
books.access_detail: Publisher, used-book, or library access
books.relevance: Supports the principles behind communication, synchronization, consistency, replication, security and fault-tolerant distributed services.
books.notes: SIGARRA supplies ISBN 0-13-613553-6, an international-edition identifier, and lists only Andrew S. Tanenbaum. Publisher/catalogue metadata attributes the work to Tanenbaum and van Steen.

books.title: Using OpenMP—The Next Step: Affinity, Accelerators, Tasking, and SIMD
books.access_detail: Publisher purchase/e-book or lawful library access
books.relevance: Provides advanced practical coverage of OpenMP affinity, accelerators, tasking and SIMD, extending CPD's shared-memory parallel-programming material.

courses.name: Artificial Intelligence
courses.status_note: 2026/2027 bibliography not treated as populated; this is the latest verified public list.

books.title: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach
books.access_detail: Commercial Pearson text or library access; the official author site lawfully provides selected chapters/preface, exercises, figures, bibliography, pseudocode and code, but not an openly licensed complete book.
books.relevance: Closely matches the IA syllabus: intelligent agents, uninformed and heuristic search, adversarial search, constraint satisfaction, logical and uncertain reasoning, planning, machine learning, reinforcement learning, NLP, perception, robotics, ethics and AI safety.
books.confidence: high for title/authors and current listing; low for any specific edition
books.notes: The current SIGARRA occurrence misspells Russell as 'Russel' and does not state an edition or ISBN. Therefore no edition can safely be assigned to FEUP's current requirement. The official author site presently describes the 4th US edition, but that must not be treated as proof that FEUP specifically requires the 4th edition.

books.title: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach
books.edition: 3rd edition, international edition identified by ISBN
books.access_detail: Commercial or library access; unauthorized PDF mirrors were rejected
books.relevance: Historical edition covering the same core agent, search, reasoning, planning, learning and NLP foundations used by IA.

books.title: Reinforcement Learning: An Introduction
books.access_detail: Publisher purchase/e-book or lawful library access
books.relevance: Directly supports IA's reinforcement-learning topics, including agents, policies, rewards, value functions, exploration versus exploitation, Markov decision processes and value-based methods.
books.notes: The historical SIGARRA page lists only Richard S. Sutton and shortens the title to 'Reinforcement learning'; MIT Press metadata confirms Andrew G. Barto as co-author and the second edition.

courses.name: Projeto Integrador
courses.status_note: 2026/2027 bibliography not treated as populated; this is the latest verified public list.

books.title: Agile Software Development with Scrum
books.access_detail: Publisher purchase/e-text, lawful used-book purchase, or library access
books.relevance: Supports PI's medium-sized team project through iterative delivery, Scrum roles, planning, inspection, adaptation and management of changing real-world requirements.
books.notes: SIGARRA lists only Ken Schwaber. Pearson and ACM bibliographic records identify Mike Beedle as co-author.

books.title: Extreme Programming Explained: Embrace Change
books.access_detail: Publisher purchase/e-text or lawful library access
books.relevance: Supports PI's collaborative software delivery with iterative planning, feedback, testing, refactoring, simple design, collective work and adaptation to changing stakeholder needs.
books.notes: SIGARRA lists only Kent Beck and abbreviates the title to 'Extreme programming explained'. The ISBN identifies the second edition, co-authored by Cynthia Andres.
